1:
The number $\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{-64}+\sqrt[3]{27}}{\sqrt[5]{-32}}$ is equal to
A. $-2$
B. $-\frac12$
C. $\frac12$
D. $2$
3:
The number $\log_5\sqrt[3]{25}$ is equal to
A. $\frac16$
B. $\frac23$
C. $\frac32$
D. $6$
7:
The figure shows the graph of a function $f$: a piecewise linear graph with domain $\langle-5,4)$, going from the point $(-5,-2)$ up to an open endpoint at $(-2,2)$, then from the filled point $(-2,0)$ up to $(2,3)$, then down to an open endpoint at $(4,-3)$. The function $f$ has exactly
A. one zero.
B. two zeros.
C. three zeros.
D. four zeros.
8:
For the piecewise linear function $f$ shown in the figure (see the previous task: from $(-5,-2)$ up to an open point at $(-2,2)$, then from $(-2,0)$ up to $(2,3)$, then down to an open point at $(4,-3)$), function $f$ attains its greatest value for the argument
A. $-2$
B. $2$
C. $3$
D. $4$
11:
The quadratic function $f$ is given by $f(x)=2x^2-kx+6$, where $k$ is a real number. The number $2$ is a zero of function $f$. The number $k$ is equal to
A. $-11$
B. $-7$
C. $7$
D. $11$
12:
The arithmetic sequence $(a_n)$ is defined for every natural number $n\ge1$. In this sequence $a_1=2$ and $a_3-a_2=-6$. The fifth term of the sequence $(a_n)$ is equal to
A. $-4$
B. $-16$
C. $-22$
D. $-28$
13:
The five-term sequence $(a_1,a_2,2,a_4,a_5)$ is geometric. The product $a_1\cdot a_2\cdot 2\cdot a_4\cdot a_5$ is equal to
A. $2$
B. $16$
C. $32$
D. $64$
14:
A right triangle has an angle $\alpha$ such that $\sin\alpha=\frac14$. The hypotenuse of this triangle has length $8$. The shorter leg of this triangle has length
A. $1$
B. $2$
C. $4$
D. $2\sqrt{15}$
15:
The angle $\alpha$ is acute and $\sin\alpha=\frac35$. The tangent of angle $\alpha$ is equal to
A. $\frac34$
B. $\frac43$
C. $\frac45$
D. $\frac54$
16:
Points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on a circle centered at $S$. Segment $BD$ is a diameter of this circle, and $|\angle ABD|=18°$. Point $D$ lies on the shorter arc $CA$ (see figure). The measure of the acute angle $BCA$ is equal to
A. $36°$
B. $60°$
C. $72°$
D. $81°$
17:
The circumference of the circle circumscribed on an equilateral triangle is equal to $16$. The height of this triangle is equal to
A. $6$
B. $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{\pi}}$
C. $12$
D. $\dfrac{12}{\pi}$
18:
The sides of an angle with vertex at point $A$ are cut by two parallel lines $k$ and $l$. Line $k$ meets the sides of the angle at points $B$ and $C$; line $l$ meets them at points $D$ and $E$. Points $B$ and $D$ lie on one side of the angle, and points $C$ and $E$ lie on the other side. Moreover $|AB|=6$, $|BC|=4$ and $|BD|=2$ (see figure). The length of segment $DE$ is equal to
A. $\frac83$
B. $\frac{16}{3}$
C. $6$
D. $8$
19:
In the coordinate plane $(x,y)$, points $A=(-3,1)$ and $B=(1,-3)$ are consecutive vertices of square $ABCD$. The perimeter of square $ABCD$ is equal to
A. $4\sqrt2$
B. $16\sqrt2$
C. $16$
D. $32$
20:
In the coordinate plane $(x,y)$, points $A=(-1,-4)$ and $B=(2,y_B)$ lie on a line $l$. The slope of line $l$ is equal to $3$. The number $y_B$ is equal to
A. $-3$
B. $5$
C. $7$
D. $-13$
21:
Every edge of a regular quadrilateral pyramid has length $12$. The height of this pyramid is equal to
A. $2\sqrt3$
B. $3\sqrt2$
C. $2\sqrt6$
D. $6\sqrt2$
22:
The slant height of a cone with base radius $1$ has length $3$. When the lateral surface of this cone is unrolled onto a plane, it forms a circular sector with a central angle of measure
A. $60°$
B. $90°$
C. $120°$
D. $150°$
23:
The number of all four-digit even natural numbers in which, in decimal notation, the thousands digit and the units digit are equal, is
A. $400$
B. $500$
C. $900$
D. $1600$
24:
In a certain town there are two schools. The first school has three times as many students as the second. The average age of students in the first school is $9$ years, and the average age of students in the second school is $13$ years. The average age of all students of both schools, expressed in years, is equal to
A. $10$
B. $10.5$
C. $11$
D. $11.5$
25:
The chart shows the results of a math test in a certain graduating class: the horizontal axis lists the grades (1 to 6) obtained by the students, and the vertical axis shows the number of students who received each grade (grade 1: 2 students, grade 2: 1, grade 3: 6, grade 4: 5, grade 5: 7, grade 6: 5). The median of the grades obtained on this test by the students of this class is equal to
A. $3$
B. $3.5$
C. $4$
D. $5$
26: Solve the equation $(27x^3+1)(x^2-4)=0$ in the set of real numbers.
29: The four-term sequence $(7, a_2, a_3, a_4)$ is arithmetic. The sum of all the terms of this sequence is equal to $54$. Compute the second term of this sequence.
31: A six-element set $K=\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}$ is given. From set $K$ we draw, without replacement, two numbers one at a time, and record them in the order drawn. Compute the probability of event $A$: the number drawn first is even, and at the same time the product of both drawn numbers is greater than $16$.
32: In the coordinate plane $(x,y)$, a parallelogram $ABCD$ is given, with $D=(6,19)$. Side $AB$ of this parallelogram lies on the line $y=\frac12x+9$, and side $AD$ lies on the line $y=4x-5$. Point $K=(10,14)$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$. The diagonals of parallelogram $ABCD$ intersect at point $S$. Compute the distance of point $S$ from the origin of the coordinate system.
33: Segment $AD$ is the height of a cylinder, and segment $AB$ is a diameter of the cylinder's base. Segment $BD$ has length $4\sqrt3$. The measure of angle $ABD$ is equal to $30°$ (see figure). Compute the volume and the total surface area of this cylinder.
34: The quadratic function $f$ is given by the formula $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$. The greatest value of function $f$ is equal to $100$. The set of all arguments for which function $f$ takes positive values is the interval $(-2,8)$. Compute the values of the coefficients $a$, $b$, and $c$.
